task.title: Say why a parsed sitemap is incomplete: truncated, entry limit exceeded, or malformed
task.body:
Why: packages/seo/docs/research/handoff-audit-unlighthouse-quality-2026-10-07.md:191 (crawl stores `sitemapsComplete=false` without the reason); packages/seo/src/domain/sitemap.ts:212-386 `parseSitemap` returns only a boolean `complete`.
Outcome: `parseSitemap(xml, maxLocEntries?)` (src/domain/sitemap.ts) returns, besides `isIndex`, `locs` and `complete`, a new field `incompleteReasons: readonly string[]` of unique codes sorted alphabetically. It is `[]` exactly when `complete` is `true`. Codes: `"entry-limit-exceeded"` when the document holds more entries than `maxLocEntries` (the entries over the limit are still not returned in `locs`, as today); `"truncated"` when the input ends (or a tag/comment/CDATA section is cut off) before the root element is closed, with no other structural error found first; `"malformed"` for any other cause of `complete === false` (wrong root, mismatched or invalid tags, bad entries, entities, namespaces) when neither of the other two codes applies. A document with both too many entries and no closing root reports both `"entry-limit-exceeded"` and `"truncated"`. `ParsedSitemap` in the same file gains the field; `locs`, `isIndex` and `complete` keep today's values for every input.
Proof: the four existing whole-object `toEqual` assertions on `parseSitemap` in tests/domain/sitemap.test.ts must be updated for the added field (an unterminated comment inside an open root is `["truncated"]`). The implementer adds own tests there for a complete file, a cut-off file, an over-limit file via a small `maxLocEntries`, and a mismatched-tag file.

spec: `parseSitemap(xml, maxLocEntries?)` (src/domain/sitemap.ts) returns, besides `isIndex`, `locs` and `complete`, a new field `incompleteReasons: readonly string[]` of unique codes sorted alphabetically. A document with both too many entries and no closing root reports both `"entry-limit-exceeded"` and `"truncated"`. `ParsedSitemap` in the same file gains the field; `locs`, `isIndex` and `complete` keep today's values for every input.

test: cd packages/seo && npx vitest run tests/hidden/hidden.test.ts
